title: Exponential Hardness of Off-Policy Evaluation under History-Dependent Logging
why_read: A theoretical result establishing exponential sample complexity lower bounds for off-policy evaluation under history-dependent logging is a rigorous but narrow contribution to reinforcement learning theory.
analysis: This is a theoretical reinforcement learning paper showing that logged datasets, even ones that visit every hidden state frequently, can still be exponentially uninformative about a target policy's value when the data-collection logger's behavior depends on history. The authors construct explicit POMDP examples proving this hardness result and match it with an optimal estimator, resolving an open hardness question posed in prior work. This is a solid piece of theory work, valuable mainly to researchers working on off-policy evaluation and reinforcement learning foundations rather than a broad engineering audience.
